notes.meaning: The Gershonites were responsible for moving all the fabric and leather parts of the tabernacle. This included the woven linen curtains, the outer animal skin coverings, the courtyard hangings, and all their ropes. They packed these items when the camp moved and set them up again when the cloud stopped.

Aaron and his sons gave the Gershonites their specific orders so that everyone knew his exact job. Aaron's son Ithamar was put in charge of overseeing their work. Having clear leadership helped prevent confusion and kept God's holy house in good order.

Moses was told to count the men in the family of Merari who were between thirty and fifty years old. This age group had the physical strength and maturity needed for tabernacle service. Serving the Lord here was seen as entering a holy army for sacred work.

The Merarites were assigned the heaviest load, including the wooden frames, crossbars, posts, and heavy bases. Moses was instructed to list every single piece by name when giving it to a worker. This careful inventory ensured that even small parts like tent pegs and ropes would not be lost.

All the labor of the Merarite clans was placed under the direction of Aaron's son Ithamar. Even though their job was heavy, physical hauling, it was necessary for God's worship. Faithful service in ordinary tasks is just as important to God as more visible roles.

Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel began the count with the Kohathite clan. They listed all the men aged thirty to fifty who were able to work at the Tent of Meeting. Only those in their prime and fit for service were chosen for this holy duty.

The Kohathite men qualified to work numbered 2,750. While many people belonged to the family, only about one third were of the right age and condition for tabernacle labor. Moses and Aaron carried out the census exactly as the Lord directed.

Next, the leaders registered the men belonging to the Gershonite families. They counted only those between thirty and fifty years of age who could handle the physical work. These were the men who carried the tabernacle curtains and coverings on the journey.

The count of able-bodied Gershonites came to 2,630 men. Like the Kohathites, only a portion of the whole family met the age requirements for service. Moses and Aaron faithfully followed God's instructions in recording every man.

The leaders counted the men of the Merarite clans using the same standard. They registered everyone from thirty to fifty years old who was fit for tabernacle duty. These workers needed strength to move the heavy wooden frames and metal bases.

The Merarites had 3,200 men fit for service. Although Merari was the smallest clan overall, more than half of their men were able to work. God provided the greatest number of strong hands to the family carrying the heaviest burden.

Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel completed the counting of all three Levite families. They registered every man between thirty and fifty years of age who was qualified to carry and maintain the tabernacle. This showed how thoroughly God organized His people for worship and travel.

The total number of Levites fit for tabernacle service was 8,580 men. Through Moses, each man was given his specific duty and load, just as the Lord had commanded. God gives each of His servants a proper place and equips them to carry out their work.
